newsitem.title: UK: Romania to launch 5-year debut mark bond next week.
newsitem.headline: Romania to launch 5-year debut mark bond next week.

text.p: Romania will launch its first mark Eurobond next week, a Romanian government official told a media briefing in London on Thursday.
"Next week we will launch our debut mark Eurobond," Finance Minister Mircea Ciumara said.
The size of the bond has been mooted around 700 million marks and is expected to have a five-year maturity.
Secretary of State Mircea Ionut Costea said the size of the deal would be for "700 million marks and up".
He said the proceeds of the bond would be used for "general government needs and (central bank's) reserves."
It is the first time the Republic of Romania will issue a Eurobond via the Ministry of Finance. In the past the National Bank of Romania was the issuing entity.
CSFB director capital markets Wolfgang Kerck said the size and pricing of the bond would be determined once investor presentations had been completed.
"The mark bond will be a benchmark for future funding exercises," Kerck said.
Romania's external debt limit was set at $3.2 billion for 1997 to be raised through the finance ministry and the central bank (BNR).
On Wednesday, central bank governor Mugur Isarescu said the BNR did not plan to tap international capital markets this year after it had raised about $1.4 billion in 1996.
Costea said Romania would consider launching either a Samurai, a Yankee or a Eurobond in another European currency in the second half of this year.
CSFB and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell are joint lead managers of the debut mark transaction.
Romania is rated Ba3 by Moody's Investors Service and BB- by Standard & Poor's.

Deutche Morgan Grenfell global markets director Peter Schikaneder said Romania had declining external debt service -- $1.02 billion in 1996, $1.34 billion in 1997, $1.45 billion in 1998 and peaking at $2.17 billion in 1999 before dropping off to $623 million in 2004. -- Hayley Pienaar, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7718
